title: The corned beef sandwich in orbit
hook: An astronaut smuggled a deli sandwich into orbit, and Congress heard about it.
peek: On the first crewed Gemini flight in 1965, John Young pulled a corned beef sandwich from his spacesuit pocket and offered it to his commander. It floated, it crumbled, and it ended up being discussed in a congressional hearing.
lede: Gemini 3 flew in March 1965 with Gus Grissom and John Young aboard, the first American spacecraft to carry two people. The crew was meant to taste-test official space food. Partway through the flight, Young produced something else: a corned beef sandwich on rye, smuggled aboard in a pocket of his spacesuit. Grissom took a bite before crumbs began drifting around the cabin.

bullets.text: The sandwich came from Wolfie's, a deli in Cocoa Beach, Florida. Fellow astronaut Wally Schirra, a famous joker, bought it and helped Young slip it aboard before launch.
Rye bread crumbles, and in weightlessness the crumbs did not fall. Loose bits could drift into instruments or be breathed in, so Grissom quickly stowed the sandwich away.

Members of the House Appropriations Committee raised the sandwich at a hearing, asking whether the stunt had spoiled a planned food experiment. NASA promised it would not happen again, and Young received a formal reprimand.
The episode showed why food in orbit had to be crumb-free. From the 1980s, crews switched to tortillas, which hold together, and that is still a staple on the International Space Station.
